title: Your First Function
story: You've been writing code inside `fn main()` for all of Level 0. But what if you could save a block of code, give it a name, and reuse it anytime you want? That's exactly what functions let you do!
why: Functions are the building blocks of every real program — they let you write code once and reuse it forever.
analogy: A function is like a named recipe — write it once, use it many times. You don't rewrite the pancake recipe every morning; you just follow the one you already have.
try_it: Add a second function called `say_bye()` that prints a goodbye message. Call both `greet()` and `say_bye()` from main.
tips: Define your function BEFORE calling it — XIOM reads top to bottom
The empty parentheses `()` after the function name mean 'this function takes no inputs'
You can call a function as many times as you want — add five `greet();` calls and watch it print five times
common_mistakes: Forgetting the parentheses when calling — `greet;` doesn't work, it must be `greet();`
Defining a function inside main — functions are defined at the top level, not nested inside other functions
